chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is a right upon the wealthy person to visit the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) twice a year, and it is a right upon the poor person to visit it once a year.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended frequency for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn for the rich and the poor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a specific spiritual duty (haqq) regarding the ziyarat of Imam al-Husayn (AS), differentiating the frequency based on financial capacity: the wealthy are encouraged to visit twice annually, while the poor are required to visit once. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on accessibility and equity in religious obligations, ensuring that the spiritual connection to the Ahl al-Bayt is maintained by all strata of society regardless of economic status. The practice underscores the enduring significance of Karbala as a central site of devotion and communal identity in Shia Islam.
